title: Solar-PV chain

chokepoint.physics: Polysilicon + wafer pulling are power- and capital-hungry, sited at cheap Chinese power

eyebrow: Product-chain pilot · the panel on the roof
h1: The whole panel is a China product — and the physics got cheaper anyway
deck: A solar module is silicon, refined into polysilicon, grown into wafers, turned into cells and laminated into panels. China makes roughly 85–98% of every one of those stages — even as the silicon needed per watt fell about eight-fold in twenty years. The chain both concentrated and dematerialised at once.
byline: silicon ≠ polysilicon (~92% CN) ≠ wafer (~98% CN) ≠ cell (~92% CN) ≠ module (~85% CN)
correction: The solar chokepoint is not a scarce element — silicon is the second-most-abundant element in the crust, and a panel uses ever less of it. The chokepoint is the factory: China holds ~92% of polysilicon, ~98% of wafers, ~92% of cells and ~85% of modules. Diversifying solar means rebuilding a manufacturing stack, not finding a deposit.

history.title: The panel dematerialised: silicon per watt, 2004 → 2024
history.note: Fraunhofer ISE. Silicon consumed per watt of cell output fell from about 16 g/W to about 2 g/W — thinner wafers, higher efficiency, diamond-wire sawing and larger ingots. Two published anchors, not an annual series. The lesson cuts against intuition: the material got radically cheaper to use, yet the chokepoint hardened — because it was never the silicon, it was the factory.

hops.t: metallurgical silicon purified to PV-grade polysilicon — ~92% China
polysilicon grown into ingots and sliced into wafers — ~98% China
wafers processed into photovoltaic cells — ~92% China
cells laminated with glass, EVA and a frame into panels — ~85% China

sections.h2: 1 · China at every stage of the chain

panels.note: IEA-PVPS. This is what total concentration looks like: not one chokepoint but a continuous one, from the purified silicon all the way to the finished panel. The module share is 'only' ~85% because final assembly is the easiest stage to move — the wafer, at ~98%, is the hard one.

panels.h3: The wafer is the real lock
panels.text: Module assembly is spreading — India, the US and Southeast Asia are building it. But wafers, at ~98% China, are the stage nobody has replicated at scale: it is capital-heavy, power-hungry and know-how-dense. A panel 'made in' another country is very often built on a Chinese wafer, so assembly shares overstate how diversified the chain really is.

sections.h2: 2 · The panel got radically more efficient

panels.text: Two decades of thinner wafers, higher cell efficiency and better sawing cut the silicon in a watt of solar roughly eight-fold. That is why panel prices collapsed and why 'silicon supply' is not the constraint — the industry keeps doing more with less of the raw material. The scarce thing is the industrial capacity to convert it, which is what concentrated.

Polysilicon and wafer production are electricity-intensive and scale-sensitive, and China combined cheap power, a decade of coordinated investment and a full upstream-to-downstream cluster. The result is the lowest-cost solar in history — and a supply chain whose every rung sits in one country. Cheap and concentrated are, here, the same fact.

The panel is not entirely China-proof of scarcity: each cell uses a little silver paste for its contacts, and PV is a meaningful slice of world silver demand — an input the industry is actively thinning (copper metallisation) but has not eliminated. It is the one genuinely material-side constraint in a chain whose main chokepoint is industrial, not geological.

trade_intro: BACI carries polysilicon, wafers, cells and modules, but a module's customs origin is its final assembly point — which increasingly hides an upstream Chinese wafer. Read the export shares below as trading positions; the true concentration is at the wafer stage, which trade data does not cleanly isolate.
